rounds.text: Vardhman Acrylics Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of 7.3x, which stands well below the sector benchmark of 15.02x [E1, E6]. Furthermore, the company’s EV/EBITDA of 5.9x is discounted relative to the sector benchmark of 8.8x [E11]. Profitability metrics powerfully support the valuation case, with an ROE of 17.1% and ROCE of 19.82% comfortably outpacing their respective sector benchmarks of 6.88% and 8.22% [E9, E10]. The balance sheet offers immense financial strength through a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and zero borrowings, complemented by a healthy dividend yield of 3.66% and a strong dividend payout of 79.3% [E4, E37, E38, E59]. Moreover, discounted cash flow modelling puts the intrinsic value at ₹ 62 per share against a market price of ₹ 41, providing a substantial margin of safety of 33.9% [E43, E44]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over 10 years sits at -3% and historical sales growth has been poor at 2.60% over the past five years [E14, E60].

A surface-level examination of Vardhman Acrylics hides deep, structural top-line stagnation, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -3%, a 5-year growth of just 3%, and a 3-year contraction of -9% [E14, E15, E16]. This secular decline translates directly into shareholder value destruction over long horizons, marked by a 10-year compounded share price growth of -1%, a 5-year return of -5%, and a 3-year return of -9% [E22, E23, E24]. Furthermore, the company's recent earnings spike is heavily flattered by non-operating factors, with earnings including a concerning other income of Rs. 14.6 Cr [E63]. Profit quality is further undermined by a weak cash conversion ratio of just 0.26x for Mar 2026, indicating that reported profits are running far ahead of actual operating cash generation due to potential receivables or accruals [E34]. Compounding these operational hurdles, the business suffers from low historical and medium-term return profiles, delivering a median ROE of just 8% over both 5-year and 3-year periods [E27, E28], alongside an inconsistent yearly operating margin trend [E32]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong balance sheet with zero debt [E37], a high dividend payout of 79.3% [E59], and a low P/E ratio of 7.3x [E1].

Conceded: 10-year compounded sales growth is -3%, 5-year growth is 3%, and 3-year growth is -9% [E14, E15, E16], alongside historical share price declines [E22, E23, E24]. However, looking backward ignores a decisive inflection in momentum, as trailing twelve month sales growth has rebounded to 12% [E17] and recent quarterly performance shows sales up 27% year-over-year [E65]. Conceded: the median ROE was 8% over 3 and 5-year periods [E27, E28], but current return metrics dramatically outperform sector benchmarks, with a robust ROCE of 19.82% versus the sector's 8.22% and a current ROE of 17.1% against 6.88% [E9, E10]. Conceded: earnings include Rs 14.6 Cr of other income [E63], but operating metrics are still fundamentally expanding, demonstrated by operating margins rising from 4% to 12% over three years [E30] and net profit surging 137% year-over-year [E67]. Conceded: cash conversion sits low at 0.26x [E34], yet the business nevertheless generated Rs 7 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 2 Cr in free cash flow while remaining completely debt-free [E35, E36, E37]. Finally, the current valuation at a P/E of 7.3x represents a heavy discount to the sector benchmark of 15.02x [E6], offering a large margin of safety where a reverse DCF shows the price already prices in negative growth [E45].

Conceded: trailing twelve month sales growth is 12% [E17] and recent quarterly sales are up 27% year-over-year [E65]. However, that short-term bounce fails to mask a severe structural decay spanning 10 years of -3% sales growth [E14], 5 years of flat 3% growth [E15], and a contracting 3-year trend of -9% [E16]. Conceded: current return metrics outpace sector medians [E9, E10], but the business exhibits chronically inconsistent operating margins over the last three years and two quarters [E32, E33], alongside a depressed 3- and 5-year median ROE of just 8% [E27, E28]. Conceded: operating metrics are expanding and profit surged 137% year-over-year [E67], but that bottom-line strength is heavily polluted by Rs 14.6 Cr of other income [E63], rendering core operating quality suspect. Conceded: the company generated Rs 7 Cr in operating cash flow [E35], but a cash conversion ratio of 0.26x reveals that reported profits are overwhelmingly detached from actual cash collection, pointing directly to severe receivables or accrual risks [E34]. Finally, conceded: the P/E sits at a low 7.3x [E6], but that discount is entirely warranted for a cyclical [E56] business with an alarming historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -85.0% [E51] and screen warnings highlighting that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E69].
